You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Tern Audio Museum","question":"Can the archive publish a channel specification?","claims":{"A":"The archive ingested a digital file from session K.","B":"The archive stored one verified copy.","C":"The master from session K is stereo."},"handoff":"The archive ingested a digital file from session K, as confirmed by intake records, and stored three verified copies rather than just one, contradicting that claim. The stereo status of the master from session K remains uncertain because although the file name includes \"stereo,\" the sender indicated the label was reused from earlier recordings. Given this uncertainty about the master’s channel configuration, the archive should be cautious about publishing a channel specification without further verification.","follow_up":{"S4":"conservator independently inspects the labelled session K master and measures distinct left/right audio channels."}}

message.content: {"claims":{"A":{"status":"supported","citations":["handoff"],"confidence":90},"B":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["handoff"],"confidence":90},"C":{"status":"unresolved","citations":["handoff"],"confidence":50}},"note":"The intake records confirm claim A that the archive ingested a digital file from session K. Claim B is contradicted by the handoff, which states the archive stored three verified copies, not one. Claim C about the master being stereo is unresolved; the file name suggests stereo but the label was reused, so the channel configuration is uncertain. The follow-up (S4) provides independent inspection confirming stereo channels, which would support claim C if considered. Overall, the archive should be cautious about publishing a channel specification without further verification."}

Claim B is contradicted by the handoff, which states the archive stored three verified copies, not one.
